title: Understanding KDE
text: Kernel Density Estimation (KDE) is a way to estimate the probability density function of a random variable. It uses kernels, which are functions centered at each data point, to smooth the distribution.

title: Role of Kernel Bandwidth
text: The kernel bandwidth, often denoted as \alpha, controls the smoothness of the KDE. A smaller \alpha results in a more wiggly estimate, while a larger \alpha gives a smoother estimate.

title: Expression for KDE
text: The KDE is calculated by summing the contributions of each kernel centered at the data points. The expression involves dividing by the number of data points, $$n$$, to normalize the estimate.
